Subject: Re: Production degradation: initial triage findings

Quick triage notes (infra view):
- Observed GPU utilization spike on FastPay's dedicated pool nodes starting 08:38 PT; sustained for >30m. Memory pressure increased and we saw frequent preemption of KV cache entries.
- A recently onboarded model variant (v3.2-fp16-large-context) is allocating larger KV buffers and higher per-request GPU time when requests include long contexts (>4k tokens).
- Continuous-batching windows for the pool automatically grew due to the traffic spike, increasing tail latencies. That, combined with KV churn, appears to be causing queueing and timeouts.

Proposed short-term mitigations (implement now):
1) Reduce batch_window_ms for FastPay's pool from 40ms -> 10ms to limit batch growth (runtime change; low risk).
2) Enable model-variant fallback for long-context requests: route >4k-token requests to a quantized v3.2-q8 variant hosted in non-dedicated capacity (falls back to hosted, preserves latency SLA for critical flows).
3) Pin KV cache sizes per-tenant to prevent cross-request eviction storms (config change; will require a rolling config rollout).

I've captured a perf dump and attached a short trace (perf-dump-fastpay-20260618.tar.gz). Will keep sampling. If we still see saturation after mitigations, we should consider a temporary reserved-throughput bump while FastPay rolls back or reduces Canary.

— Sergio
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
